title: Clopidogrel with or without omeprazole in coronary artery disease
authors: Bhatt DL, Cryer BL, Contant CF, Cohen M, Lanas A, Schnitzer TJ, et al.
followUp: event rates at 180 days; terminated early when the sponsor lost financing
population: Patients with an indication for dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel; 3761 included in analyses
funder: Funded by Cogentus Pharmaceuticals (statement in the abstract). Registry NCT00557921: lead sponsor Cogentus Pharmaceuticals; responsible party Pablo Lapuerta, Cogentus Pharmaceuticals, an author; intervention CGT-2168, clopidogrel 75 mg with omeprazole 20 mg, against clopidogrel 75 mg; terminated by the sponsor.
result: Gastrointestinal events 1.1% with omeprazole against 2.9% with placebo at 180 days (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.63); overt upper gastrointestinal bleeding HR 0.13 (0.03 to 0.56). Cardiovascular events 4.9% against 5.7% (HR 0.99, 0.68 to 1.44). Diarrhoea was more frequent with omeprazole.
